[LRST.1.4] `<expr>` must evaluate to a scalar value that admits
equality. The legal types are `String`, `Int`, `Float`, `Bool`, `Date`,
`Time`, `Duration` and `Bytes`, and no other. The compiler must reject
`as <expr>` of any other type with `DS_VALIDATE_AS_NON_EQUATABLE_TYPE`. A
`call`'s key is narrower still: a `String` only ([LRST.1.4.1]). A
`Json` value is a document, not a scalar key, so an author projects a typed
leaf first. An interval, a fact reference and an opaque value name nothing a
later firing can match as a key.

Two keys of one declaration are the same key exactly when `==` between them is
`true`. So `-0.0` and `0.0` are one key; a NaN is the same key as nothing, and
supersedes nothing ([LEXP.4.2]); and two `Time` values are one key when they
denote the same UTC instant, whatever their offsets ([LTIM.5.2]).
